# Regular expressions and Languages

* Regular Languages: simplest family of Formal Languages

* Regular Expressions: starting string & containing various types of operators

* A language is regular if it is generated by a Regular Expression

## FAMILY OF REGULAR LANGUAGES (REG)
* is the collection of all regular languages

## FAMILY OF FINITE LANGUAGES (FIN)
* is the collection of all languages of finite cardinality (that contain only finitely many strings)

* Caution: REG and FIN are sets of sets of strings, not sets of strings themselves

* EVERY FINITE LANGUAGE IS REGULAR, because it is the (finite) union of finitely many strings, and each string is in turn the concatenation of finitely many letters or in general of alphabetic symbols

* But the family of regular languages also contains many (actually infinitely many) languages of infinite cardinality (that contain infinitely many strings)

* FIN $\subset$ REG

## Operators
* Union

* Concatenation

* Star

* Power: $e^k$

* Repetition: $e^+$

* Optionality: $e?$

## Closure of Regular Languages
* Let $\otimes$ be an operator that produces another language (result), when it is applied to one language (one operand) or to a pair of languages (two operands)

* A FAMILY OF LANGUAGES IS SAID TO BE CLOSED WITH RESPECT TO AN OPERATOR $\otimes$, IF THE RESULT LANGUAGE BELONGS TO THE SAME FAMILY AS THE OPERAND LANGUAGE(S)

* PROPERTY: the family REG of the regular languages is CLOSED with respect to the following operators: concatenation, union and star; therefore REG is closed also w.r.t. the derived operators, i.e. cross, repetition, optionality, etc.

* THE MEANING OF A REGEXP is a language L over the alphabet $\Sigma$

* A LANGUAGE IS REGULAR if it is the meaning (if it is generated) by a regular expression

## Linguistic Abstraction
* the smallest family of languages such that both the following properties hold:

  * REG contains all finite languages
  * REG closed w.r.t. concatenation, union and star
* AT THE ABSTRACT LEVEL THE TYPICAL STRUCTURES OF MOST ARTIFICIAL LANGUAGES CAN BE OBTAINED BY THE COMPOSITION OF FEW ELEMENTARY PARADIGMS, AND BY THE BASIC LANGUAGE OPERATIONS SUCH AS CONCATENATION, UNION AND ITERATION

## Lists
* A list is a sequence of a number of elements, not fixed in advance

* A list can be generated by the regexp $e^+$ or $e^*$, if the empty list is admitted

* The element e can be a terminal (alphabetic symbol) or a compound object of some kind (for instance, a list itself)

* LISTS WITH SEPARATORS AND START-MARKER OR END-MARKER

* Lists may contain atomic objects as elements, but also other lists of lower level

* EXAMPLES:

  * level 1: begin istr istr istr end
  * level 2: STAMPA(var, var... var)

## Substitution
* SUBSTITUTION (REPLACEMENT): operation that replaces the terminal characters of the source language with the phrases of the target (or destination) language
